title: Direct summands of perfect complexes are perfect
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let K and L be objects of the derived category D(\mathcal{O}_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. If K is isomorphic to a direct sum L \oplus M for some object M and K is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], then L is perfect (and likewise M is perfect).

proof.text: Reuse the existing private hasDerivedCategory_of_equivalence theorem from SchemeIsoDerivedLocalizations via import all. Transport the chosen derived localizations from localized open sites to open subschemes through Modules.overEquiv without increasing the Hom universe; the reused helper constructs this localization explicitly.
Apply lem-pc-perfect-pseudo-coherent-locally-finite-tor to obtain pseudo-coherence and local Tor bounds for K; apply lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-summand to obtain pseudo-coherence of L and M.

Compose the biproduct inclusions and projections with the isomorphism K = L plus M to form retracts of K. Derived open pullback preserves these retract equations. On each Tor neighbourhood, apply lem-pc-derived-tensor-vanishing-retract degree by degree to retain the same interval for each summand.
Apply lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-locally-finite-tor-perfect to each summand, using its pseudo-coherence and the local Tor bounds just proved.

proof_origin.note: Q1 Lean reduction: explicit derived retracts and local affine finite-projective construction; one local affine Tor-transfer hole. Second reading removes the copied localization helper and reuses SchemeIsoDerivedLocalizations.hasDerivedCategory_of_equivalence.
